objection: I checked every step and found no gap. (a): the integration by parts on each interval (n,n+1) and the telescoped sum -4Σ_{m≤N} m^{1/2}+2N^{1/2}+(8/3)N^{3/2} are correct. The Euler–Maclaurin continuation at s=-1/2 gives Σ_{m≤N} m^{1/2} = ζ(-1/2)+(2/3)N^{3/2}+(1/2)N^{1/2}+O(N^{-1/2}), so I = -4ζ(-1/2) = 0.8315448999094, which I confirmed numerically. (b): the identity B(x) = x - x^2 + 2Σ_k (x-k)_+ is correct. The EM boundary and remainder terms E_1 to E_5 are computed correctly; the integrals ∫6Z/u^4 = 2Z/T^3 and ∫20Z^2/u^6 = 4Z^2/T^5 are right, and G_k'(R_k) = -2k^{3/2}/√Z. The bounds from (b.1) follow from Λ/2 < T ≤ Λ, and the k-count is below K_0 < 4Λ. The total of about 56.1Λ, plus at most Λ/2 for s ≤ T, stays under 60Λ. The case Z<1 is handled separately and is fine. A numerical check over Z in (0,30] and Z up to about 10^9 gives |error|/Z^{1/3} ≤ 0.32. (c): the values of b = μ*f at prime powers are correct. Σ|b(d)|d^{-2/3} ≤ C_1·2^{ω(q)} with C_1 absolute, and Σ|b(d)|/d < ∞ for each fixed q, which justifies the interchange of summation. Applying (b) at Z/d^2 for every d is allowed because (b) holds for every Z>0. The Euler-product identity Σb(d)/d = δ_q checks out: (p^3-3p+2) = (p-1)^2(p+2). The implied constant c_1·C_1·sup_q 2^{ω(q)}q^{-ε} depends only on ε. Ranges and uniformity match the statement exactly, and no result from 2011 or later is used.
